subject: English
passage: One established principle of hospitality is that the effort invested in preparing a meal will be viewed as a reflection of the host's care for their guests. Culinary researchers Omolara Abiodun, Danilo Ramos, and Sarah Williams examined this belief in their studies of attitudes specifically surrounding meal preparation methods, noting that while diners tend to view meals prepared using modern appliances (which can reduce cooking time significantly and often require minimal supervision) as superior to meals prepared using traditional methods (which typically demand more hands-on time and constant attention) in terms of consistency and flavor, 91.2 percent of participants surveyed indicated that it is more meaningful to serve a meal prepared using traditional methods. This finding suggests that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: hosts likely perceive modern appliances as requiring relatively little effort to use and thus wrongly assume guests will value meals prepared with them less than they do traditionally prepared meals.
choices.B: hosts likely overestimate the complexity of using modern appliances and thus mistakenly assume guests will view meals prepared with them as less impressive than traditionally prepared meals.
choices.C: traditionally prepared meals are likely preferred by diners because the artisanal nature of those methods offers a greater emotional connection than modern appliances do.
choices.D: traditionally prepared meals are likely less desirable to diners than modern appliance-prepared meals are because of the perception that traditional methods involve excessive labor.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it most logically completes the text's discussion of perceptions of modern versus traditional meal preparation methods. The text begins by explaining that the perception of "the effort invested in preparing a meal…as a reflection of the host's care" is an established principle of hospitality. The text then explains that although diners view meals prepared with modern appliances as superior to traditionally prepared meals in terms of consistency and flavor, a culinary study nonetheless showed that 91.2% of participants found traditionally prepared meals more "meaningful" to serve. The text specifically contrasts how modern appliances "can reduce cooking time significantly and often require minimal supervision" with the fact that traditional methods "typically demand more hands-on time and constant attention"—suggesting the greater effort required by traditional preparation. Given the text's initial premise that hospitality norms equate the care shown to guests with the effort involved in meal preparation, it is reasonable to infer that people perceive modern appliances as requiring less effort to use and thus assume guests will value those meals less, even though diners actually prefer meals prepared with modern appliances for their superior consistency and flavor.
